module_triggers.include_when: The service can create, change or approve payments, orders, trades, holdings or client-asset records.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Can the service affect payments, trades or client assets?" → Yes

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor hosts, operates or stores anything for the client on cloud or vendor-controlled infrastructure.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Where does the service run?" → Vendor-hosted or cloud
module_triggers.note: Renamed from "Cloud & Hosting" in bank version 3, to tell it apart from the base domain "Cloud & Hosting Security"

module_triggers.include_when: Vendor staff hold production, database, admin or security-tool access.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Access to client systems" → Privileged or admin

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor receives, stores or can access personal data, including employee data.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Data the vendor handles" → Personal data or higher

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor develops, supplies, deploys or maintains software or APIs the client uses.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Does the vendor supply software or APIs?" → Yes

module_triggers.include_when: Client data sits at vendor or subcontractor facilities, or vendor staff work on client premises.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "Client data at vendor sites, or vendor staff on client premises?" → Yes

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor supplies software that is installed and run in the client's own environment (the vendor does not host it).
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "How is the service delivered?" → Software installed in the client's environment. Also switches the Base set to rows tagged Client-hosted.

module_triggers.include_when: DRAFT: vendor developers or other staff work inside the client's environment (client devices, virtual desktops, repositories).
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "How is the service delivered?" → Vendor staff work inside the client's environment. Base set becomes the 8 rows tagged Staff in client environment.

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor answers Yes to AIS-01 (AI will be used to provide the scoped services), or the consultant adds it.
module_triggers.trigger: Vendor answer to AIS-01 = Yes. AIM-08 = Yes raises the tier to at least High. A later model or provider change triggers an early reassessment.

module_triggers.include_when: The vendor provides a service that is not technology: facilities, housekeeping, security guards, staffing, couriers, call centres, printing, consultants.
module_triggers.trigger: Criticality Q: "How is the service delivered?" → Non-technology service. Base set becomes the 17 rows tagged Non-technology services, for every tier; add the Personal Data module if the vendor handles personal data.

glossary.CISO: Chief information security officer: the executive responsible for information security.
glossary.ISMS: Information security management system: the policies and processes an organisation uses to manage information security.
glossary.RACI: Responsible, accountable, consulted, informed: a matrix showing who does what for each task.
glossary.SLA: Service level agreement: a committed level of service, such as a response time.
glossary.PAM: Privileged access management: tools that control and record administrator access.
glossary.TLS: Transport Layer Security: the standard encryption for data sent over a network.
glossary.HSM: Hardware security module: a tamper-resistant device that stores and uses encryption keys.
glossary.KMS: Key management service: a service that creates, stores and controls encryption keys.
glossary.VPN: Virtual private network: an encrypted connection into a private network.
glossary.DDoS: Distributed denial of service: an attack that floods a service with traffic to make it unavailable.
glossary.OWASP: Open Worldwide Application Security Project: a non-profit that publishes widely used lists of web and AI application risks.
glossary.DR: Disaster recovery: restoring systems and data after a serious disruption.
glossary.CSPM: Cloud security posture management: tools that check cloud settings against a security baseline.
glossary.MFA: Multi-factor authentication: signing in with a second proof as well as a password, such as a code or a security key.
glossary.OEM: Original equipment manufacturer: the company that makes a product, as opposed to one that resells or supports it.
glossary.SBOM: Software bill of materials: a list of the components and libraries inside a piece of software.
glossary.SIEM: Security information and event management: a system that collects logs and raises security alerts.
glossary.WORM: Write once, read many: storage that cannot be changed or deleted once written.
glossary.API: Application programming interface: a way for one system to exchange data with another.
glossary.EDR: Endpoint detection and response: software on laptops and servers that detects and responds to attacks.
glossary.MDM: Mobile device management: software that controls and secures phones and tablets.
glossary.RCA: Root cause analysis: finding the underlying cause of an incident.
glossary.RTO: Recovery time objective: how quickly a service must be restored after a disruption.
glossary.RPO: Recovery point objective: the most data, measured in time, that may be lost after a disruption.
glossary.CCTV: Closed-circuit television: security cameras that record a site.
glossary.ISO/IEC 27001: The international standard for information security management systems.
glossary.SOC 2: System and Organization Controls 2: an independent auditor's report on a service organisation's security controls.
glossary.ISO 27701: The international standard that extends ISO 27001 to privacy management.
glossary.ISO 22301: The international standard for business continuity management.
glossary.PCI DSS: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard: the security standard for organisations that handle card data.
glossary.CSA STAR: Cloud Security Alliance Security, Trust, Assurance and Risk: a registry of cloud providers' security assessments.
glossary.LLM: Large language model: an AI model that reads and writes text.
glossary.AIBOM: AI bill of materials: a list of the models, datasets and software components behind an AI system.
glossary.ISO/IEC 42001: The international standard for AI management systems.
glossary.ISO 27001: The international standard for information security management systems.
glossary.L2/L3: Second-line and third-line support: technical support levels above the first help desk.
glossary.SSO: Single sign-on: signing in once to reach several systems.
glossary.AD: Active Directory: Microsoft's directory service that holds user accounts and groups for signing in.
glossary.LDAP: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol: a standard way to look up users and groups in a directory.
glossary.SAML: Security Assertion Markup Language: a standard for single sign-on.
glossary.OIDC: OpenID Connect: a standard for signing in with an identity provider.
glossary.CSP: Cloud service provider: a company that provides cloud hosting or platforms, for example AWS, Azure or Google Cloud.
glossary.PIM: Privileged identity management: granting administrator rights only when needed and for a limited time.
glossary.VM: Virtual machine: a computer run as software on shared hardware.
glossary.RoPA: Record of processing activities: a register of how an organisation processes personal data.
glossary.DPIA: Data protection impact assessment: an assessment of privacy risks before processing personal data.
glossary.SPDX: Software Package Data Exchange: a standard format for software bills of materials.
glossary.SCA: Software composition analysis: tools that find known weaknesses and licences in open-source components.
glossary.EOL: End of life: no longer supported by its maker, so it gets no security fixes.
glossary.CI/CD: Continuous integration and continuous delivery: the automated pipeline that builds, tests and releases software.
glossary.SAST: Static application security testing: checking source code for security weaknesses without running it.
glossary.DAST: Dynamic application security testing: testing a running application for security weaknesses.
glossary.NAV: Net asset value: the value of a fund's assets less its liabilities.
glossary.DORA: Digital Operational Resilience Act: the EU regulation on ICT risk and resilience for financial entities.
glossary.TLPT: Threat-led penetration testing: a test that simulates a real attacker, based on current threat intelligence.
glossary.LEI: Legal Entity Identifier: a 20-character code that identifies a company in financial transactions.
glossary.EEA: European Economic Area: the EU countries plus Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway.
glossary.SCCs: Standard contractual clauses: the EU's standard contract terms for sending personal data outside the EEA.
glossary.BCRs: Binding corporate rules: approved internal rules that let a group of companies move personal data between its own countries.
glossary.NIS2: The EU directive on the security of network and information systems (the second version).
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India: India's central bank and banking regulator.
glossary.SEBI: Securities and Exchange Board of India: India's securities market regulator.
glossary.IRDAI: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India: India's insurance regulator.
glossary.PFRDA: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority: India's pension regulator.
glossary.CERT-In: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team: India's national agency for cyber security incidents.
glossary.IFSCA: International Financial Services Centres Authority: the regulator of India's International Financial Services Centre.
glossary.IFSC: International Financial Services Centre: India's financial centre at GIFT City.
glossary.GIFT City: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City: the location of India's International Financial Services Centre.
glossary.AML: Anti-money laundering: controls that detect and prevent money laundering.
glossary.KYC: Know your customer: checks that confirm a customer's identity.
glossary.MeitY: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology: the Indian government ministry for IT.
glossary.STQC: Standardisation Testing and Quality Certification: an Indian government directorate that audits IT services.
glossary.NIC: National Informatics Centre: the Indian government's technology organisation, which runs national time servers.
glossary.NPL: National Physical Laboratory: India's national measurement laboratory, which keeps Indian Standard Time.
glossary.NTP: Network Time Protocol: the standard way computers keep their clocks in step.
glossary.VPS: Virtual private server: a rented virtual machine on a provider's hardware.
glossary.DPDP: Digital Personal Data Protection: India's data protection law (the DPDP Act, 2023).
glossary.QSA: Qualified Security Assessor: an auditor approved to assess compliance with PCI DSS.
glossary.SAQ D: Self-Assessment Questionnaire D: the PCI DSS self-assessment form for service providers.
glossary.NPS: National Pension System: India's pension scheme, run under PFRDA and the NPS Trust.
glossary.CSCRF: Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework: SEBI's cyber security framework for regulated entities in India's securities market.
glossary.SDAIA: Saudi Data and AI Authority: Saudi Arabia's data protection regulator.
glossary.SAMA: Saudi Central Bank: the financial regulator of Saudi Arabia.
glossary.MAS: Monetary Authority of Singapore: Singapore's central bank and financial regulator.
glossary.APEC: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation: a forum of Pacific Rim economies that runs the CBPR privacy certification.
glossary.CBPR: Cross-Border Privacy Rules: a privacy certification for companies that move personal data between participating countries.
glossary.PRP: Privacy Recognition for Processors: the APEC privacy certification for companies that process data for others.
glossary.PDPC: Personal Data Protection Commission: Singapore's data protection regulator.
glossary.CBUAE: Central Bank of the UAE: the banking regulator of the United Arab Emirates.
glossary.DIFC: Dubai International Financial Centre: a financial free zone in Dubai with its own data protection law.
glossary.ADGM: Abu Dhabi Global Market: a financial free zone in Abu Dhabi with its own data protection law.
glossary.CTP: Critical third party: a provider designated by the UK government as critical to the UK financial sector.
glossary.PRA: Prudential Regulation Authority: a UK financial regulator, part of the Bank of England.
glossary.FCA: Financial Conduct Authority: a UK financial regulator.
glossary.IDTA: International data transfer agreement: the UK's standard contract for sending personal data abroad.
glossary.DPF: Data Privacy Framework: the EU-US arrangement under which certified US companies can receive personal data from the EU.
glossary.FTC: Federal Trade Commission: a US federal regulator for consumer protection.
glossary.PHI: Protected health information: health data about a person that US health privacy law protects.
glossary.DFS: New York State Department of Financial Services: the financial services regulator of New York State.
